s: puM, (gareRa saha varttamAnaH .) arhadBedaH । iti hemacandraH ॥ sUryyavaMSIyarAjaviSezaH । sa tu ayoDyADipatibAhurAjaputtraH tasyotpattyAdi yaTA, -- sUryyavaMSe mahArAjI bAhurnAma mahAnaBUt । tasya rAjyaM hftaM sarvvaM hEhayEstAlajaNGakEH ॥ kAmbojAH pahravAScEva pAradA yavanAH SakAH । ete paYcagaRA brahman hEhayArTe parAkraman ॥ hftarAjyaH sa vE vipra tadA bAhurvvanaM yayO । patnI tu yAdavI tasya gurvviRyAsIt pativratA ॥ tatsapatnI pUrvvameva tasyA garBajiGAMsayA । Bojanena saha prAdAt garaM DarmmAnavekzayA ॥ yAdavyAstu tapoyogAt garBo mEva mamAra ha । na mamAra ca sA rAjYI devAnAmanukampayA ॥ patiM sAnuyayO sADvI sizeve taM vane sadA ! sa rAjA vipine tasmin prARAMstatyAja yogavAn ॥ sA tu BarttuScitiM kftvA vane tAmaDyarohata । OrvvastAM BArgavastAta kAruRyAt samavArayat ॥ tasyASrame ca sA garBaM suzuve jvalanapraBam । vyajAyata mahAbAhurgareREva saha dvija ॥ sagaro nAma tenABUt bAlako'timanoharaH । Orvastu jAtakarmmAdi tasya kftvA mahAtmanaH ॥ aDyApya vedAnaKilAn SastrARi pratyapAdayat । Agneyantu mahAGoramamarErapi duHsaham ॥ sa tenAstrabalenAjO balena ca samanvitaH ! hEhayAMstAlajaNGAMSca jaGna rudraH paSUniva ॥ janayAmAsa loke'smin kIrttiM kIrtti matAMvaraH tataH SakAn sayavanAn kAmbojAn pAradAMstaTA । pahravAMScApi niHSezAn karttuM vyavasito nfpaH ॥ te hanyamAnA vAreRa sagareRa mahIjasA । vaSizWaM SaraRaM jagmuH sUryyavaMSapurohitam ॥ vaSizWaH SaraRApannAn samaye sTApya tAnfziH । sagaraM vArayAmAsa teByA dattvABayaM tadA ॥ sagarastAM prAMtajYAntu niSamya sumahAbalaH । DarmmaM jaGAna tezAYca veSAnanyAMScakAra ha ॥ ardDaM SiraH SakAnAntu muRqayAmAsa BUpatiH । yavanAnAM SiraH sarvvaM kAmbAjAnAmapi dvija ॥ pAradAn muktakeSAstu pahravAn SmaSruDAriRaH । nisvADyAyavazawkArAn sarvvAneva cakAraha ॥ kAlisarpA mAhizakA dArvvAScolAH sakeralAH KasAstuzArAScInASca madrAH kizkinDakAstaTA । kontalASca taTA banDAH SAmbAH koNkaRakAstaTA । sarvve te kzattriyAstAta DarmmAstezAM nirAkftAH ॥ purAhitasya vAkyana kftA vikftaveSinaH । vaSa kftya sarAjanyAn svarAjyamanvaSAsata ॥” iti pAdme svargaKaRqe 15 aDyAyaH ॥ * ॥ api ca । “rohitAcca vfko jAto vfkAdvAhurajAyata ॥ sagarastasya puttro'BUt rAjA paramaDArmmikaH ॥ dve BAryye sagarasyApi praBA BAnumatI taTA । tAByAmArADitaH pUrvva mOrvvo'gniH puttrakAmyayA OrvvastuzwastuyAH prAdAt yaTezwaM varamuttamam । ekA zazwisahasrARi sutamekaM taTA parA ॥ gfhRAtu vaMSakarttAraM praBA gfhRAdbahUM staTA । ekaM BAnumatIputtramagfhRAdasamaYjasam ॥ tataH zazwisahasrARi suzuve yAdavI praBA । KanantaH pfTivIM dagDA vizRunA ye'SvamArgaRe ॥ asamaYjasastu tanayaH aMSumAn nAma viSrutaH । tasya puttro dilIpastu dilIpAttu BagIraTaH ॥ yena BAgIraTI gaNgA tapaH kftvAvatAritA । BagIrayasya tanayo nABAga iti viSrutaH ॥” iti mAtsye 12 aDyAyaH ॥
v: pu॰ saha gareRa vizeRa jAtaH । 1 sUryyavaMSye nfpaBede “sagarAt sAgarojAtaH” iti purARam । sa ca subAhunAmarAjataH yAdavyAM jAtaH tatasapatnyA garadAne'pi sa na samAra tatkaTA “tasyA (OrvasyA) Srame ca sA gaBaM suzuve jvalanapraBam । vyajAyata mahAbAhurgareREva saha dvija! । sagaro nAma tenABUt bAlako'timanoharaH” padmapu॰ 13 a॰ । 2 vizayukte tri॰ ।

N. of a king of the solar race, sovereign of Ayodhyā (son of Bāhu; he is said to have been called Sa-gara, as born together with a poison given to his mother by the other wife of his father; he was father of Asamañja by Keśinī and of sixty thousand sons by Su-mati; the latter were turned into a heap of ashes by the sage Kapila [see भगीरथ], and their funeral ceremonies could only be performed by the waters of Gaṅgā to be brought from heaven for the purpose of purifying their remains ; this was finally accomplished by the devotion of Bhagīratha, who having led the river to the sea, called it Sāgara in honour of his ancestor: Sagara is described as having subdued the Śakas, Yavanas, and other barbarous tribes; pl. ‘the sons of Sagara’), MBh.; R. &c. (IW. 361)
N. of a partic. Arhat, MW.
सगर m. and f(आ). (for 1. 2. स-ग्˚ See col. 1) night (?), TS. : ŚBr. (in a formula).
a: सगर — a. [गरेण विषेण सहितः] Poisonous, having poison. --रः N. of a king of the Solar race. [He was a son of Bāhu and was called Sagara because he was born together with gara or poison given to his mother by the other wife of his father. By his wife Sumati he had 60000 sons. He successfully performed 99 sacrifices, but when he commenced the hundredth, his sacrificial horse was stolen by Indra and carried down to the Pātāla. Sagara thereupon commanded his 60000 sons to search it out. Finding no trace of the animal on earth they began to dig down towards the Pātāla, and in doing this they naturally increased the boundaries of the ocean which was therefore called Sāgara; cf. R. 13. 3. Meeting with the sage Kapila they rashly accused him of having stolen their horse, as a punishment for which they were instantly reduced to ashes by that sage. It was after several thousands of years that Bhagīratha (q. v.) succeeded in bringing down to the Pātāla the celestial river Ganges to water and purify their ashes and thus to convey their souls to heaven].
